PullRequest.Title: Report failed and cancelled subagent turn outcomes
PullRequest.Body:
When the host closes a subagent's child turn on the task-list path, it always records the turn as `success`: `completeSubagentSession` in `agentSideEffects.ts` dispatches `ChatTurnComplete` and calls `_completeTurn(..., 'success')`. A `task` subagent whose task ends as `failed` or `cancelled` therefore shows a completed child turn with no error in the UI, and `agentHost.turnCompleted` reports it as `success`. The same applies to an inline subagent the runtime tears down, which sends `subagent.completed` with `cancelled: true`. #339619 fixed this only for `subagent.failed` on subagents with no task.

## Telemetry

Last 3 days, `copilotcli` provider. Each child `agenthost.turncompleted` is joined (by `parenttoolcallid`) to the `copilotsdk/tool_call_executed` event of the tool call that spawned it. The tool's `result_type` is the actual outcome.

**`task` subagents:**

| Tool result | Child turn recorded as | Child turns | Devices |
|---|---|---|---|
| FAILURE | `error` | 1,977 | 727 |
| FAILURE | **`success`** | **652** | **134** |
| FAILURE | `cancelled` | 81 | 3 |
| SUCCESS | `success` | 190,290 | 17,680 |

- **24% of failed sync `task` subagents (652 of 2,710) are recorded as `success`**, about 0.3% of all `task` subagent turns. The `task` subagent failure rate is therefore understated by about a quarter.
- The two failure groups look different. Turns already recorded as `error` mostly failed at startup: 77% made zero model calls, with a median of 3 s. The child's own `session.error` already ends those as errors. Turns recorded as `success` did real work first (median 3 model calls, 28 s), then failed through a `failed` task status or `subagent.failed`. That is the path this PR fixes.
- This is a lower bound. A background `task` call reports `SUCCESS` as soon as the agent launches, so later background failures can't be counted this way.
- The behavior is the same on stable 1.135–1.140 and 1.141 Insiders, so it is long-standing, not a regression.

## Fix

The host now reports how the subagent ended before it closes the child turn:

- **Task status `failed`**: emit a child-scoped `ChatError` (`errorType: 'subagentFailed'`). The message and duration come from a pending `subagent.failed` when there is one, and otherwise from the task's `error` and `activeTimeMs`.
- **Task status `cancelled`**, or **`subagent.completed` with `cancelled: true`** on a subagent with no task: emit a child-scoped `ChatTurnCancelled`.
- **Task status `idle` / `completed`**: unchanged, recorded as `success`.

The outcome is emitted only while the subagent is still active, so a turn the host already closed through its own abort path is not reported twice. Side effects remap the action onto the child turn and record `error` or `cancelled`. The `subagent_completed` that follows then finds no active turn and does nothing.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The changed task-status path, child-action routing, and downstream contribution calls are explicit. Subagent starts bypass the normal send/checkpoint-start path, but the contribution still schedules session and branch changeset recomputes, and the Git-state contributor still runs. Exact wall-clock cost varies by repository size and whether failures overlap enough to coalesce, which affects severity rather than mechanism confidence.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Git subprocesses, diff-worker/database operations, and Git-state refresh work
Findings.PerformanceScaling: For K task-backed subagent failures, staggered failures trigger K full child error turn-end pipelines. Same-strategy requests coalesce only while a recompute is already pending; a single failure can still enqueue both the immediate fileEditTracker session recompute and the post-checkpoint auto recompute because they use different strategies. Branch recomputation can fan out across repositories with concurrency capped at five.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Repeated background Git/diff/database work consumes CPU and I/O, reduces agent-host throughput, and can delay legitimate checkpoint and Git-state work for the parent session.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before this change, a task whose status became failed was finalized through `_completeSubagentTurn`; `completeSubagentSession` dispatched a child `ChatTurnComplete` and directly called `_completeTurn`, without invoking the generic chat-contribution `turnEnd` pipeline.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The new failed outcome emits `ChatError` before `subagent_completed`. AgentSideEffects routes that action to the child chat and invokes every `onTurnEnd` contribution, including workspace-wide checkpoint/changeset and GitHub-reference processing.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT line 1963 adds the child `ChatError` emitted by `_emitSubagentOutcome`; the same diff replaces the old terminal-task `_completeSubagentTurn(...)` call with `_settleSubagentTurn(..., this._taskOutcome(task))`, moving task failures into the generic error turn-end fan-out.
Findings.Title: Skip workspace-wide turn-end work for failed subagents
Findings.Impact: When an agent workflow has one or more task-backed subagents fail, each failure now starts parent-workspace recomputation that is unrelated to reporting the child outcome. In a multi-repository session this can launch Git diff work across repositories; repeated or staggered failures repeat that work and contend with the active parent workflow.
Findings.Evidence: `_taskOutcome` turns a terminal task status into `kind: 'failed'`, and this added `ChatError` reaches `AgentSideEffects._dispatchActionForSession`, whose error branch calls `_chatContributions.turnEnd`. `CheckpointAndChangesetContribution.onTurnEnd` accepts non-resumable errors, calls `changesets.onTurnComplete`, then calls `refreshSessionChangeset(..., 'auto')`; `AgentHostChangesetService.onTurnComplete` already schedules branch and containing-session recomputes with `fileEditTracker`. `_scheduleStaticRecompute` only replaces adjacent requests with the same strategy, so the fileEditTracker and auto requests are distinct. `GitHubReferencesContribution.onTurnEnd` also calls `attachSessionGitHubPullRequest`, which refreshes Git state. None of this pipeline ran for task-backed failed statuses before the changed `_settleSubagentTurn` path.
Findings.Recommendation: Keep emitting and persisting the child error for state and telemetry, but prevent Tool-origin/subagent chats from running workspace-wide turn-end contributors such as checkpoint/changeset and GitHub-reference refresh. Alternatively add a child-outcome flag that those contributors can gate on; preserve the lightweight child completion/error lifecycle.

Scenarios.Scenario: A task-backed subagent reaches failed status during a parent agent workflow
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The per-agent quiet-period scheduler calls the existing background-task reconciliation RPC and awaits `tasks.list`; once the failed snapshot is authoritative, the changed path synchronously emits the child `ChatError` and completes child state. Workspace recomputes, database persistence, and Git/GitHub refreshes are fire-and-forget after action dispatch, so they are off the immediate UI completion path but contend with subsequent parent-session work.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Copilot SDK `rpc.tasks.list()` reads the authoritative background-task snapshot.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One read per accepted reconciliation; overlapping refreshes are throttled/serialized and superseded revisions are discarded.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same reconciliation and task-list RPC determined terminal child status before this PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited before the child can settle after the quiet period.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Serializes the failed child turn and inserts a persisted-turn record.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One insert per newly reported task-backed failed child; per-chat sequencing does not coalesce distinct child chats.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Task-backed failed statuses were closed as success and did not enter the error `turnEnd` contribution, so no failed-turn insert occurred.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Fire-and-forget and off the immediate child completion path, but adds database/serialization load.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Schedules parent session/branch changeset recomputation, including DB/diff-worker scans and Git diff subprocesses where Git-backed strategies apply.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: A failure schedules an immediate fileEditTracker recompute and a post-checkpoint auto recompute; branch work is also scheduled. Same-strategy requests can coalesce during overlap, but different strategies and staggered failures remain separate; multi-root fan-out is capped at five repositories concurrently.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The old task-status path called `_completeSubagentTurn` and bypassed chat-contribution `turnEnd`, so these workspace-wide recomputes were not scheduled for task-backed failures.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Asynchronous after child state completion, but consumes the same host CPU/I/O and sequencers used by later parent-session checkpoint and changeset work.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Refreshes repository Git state and may resolve the branch's pull request through GitHub.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One trigger per failed child; per-session throttling/serialization bounds overlapping triggers, while failures outside the throttle window repeat repository queries and unresolved branch lookups.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Task-backed failed statuses did not invoke this `turnEnd` contribution.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Fire-and-forget from `turnEnd`; background Git/network work can delay later queued refreshes.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number K of task-backed child failures in a session, repository count R, tracked edit/history size, and repository size. Same-strategy recomputes may coalesce during a tight burst, but staggered failures repeat work; multi-root Git work is limited to min(R, 5) concurrent repository operations.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Background-task RPC reads are serialized/coalesced by `_backgroundTaskStatusRefreshThrottler`; completion timers are per child. Changeset jobs serialize by session/kind and only coalesce adjacent requests with the same strategy, while multi-repository work uses a limiter of five. Git-state refresh is throttled per session with a five-second window. Failed-turn persistence is sequenced per child chat.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Task outcomes use existing in-memory task snapshots and pending lifecycle maps, which are deleted on completion. Changeset state is retained, but terminal recomputes are still scheduled; fileEditTracker and auto requests do not coalesce because their strategy keys differ. Git state is cached, although each accepted refresh still queries the repository before comparing it. No negative-cache change was introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed failed-task path, child action routing, unconditional `turnEnd` fan-out, and downstream boundary implementations are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact cost depends on repository size, enabled changeset state, failure spacing, and whether GitHub association is already resolved. Tight bursts coalesce some work, while sequential failures do not.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable boundary fan-out: preserving the child error outcome now also starts unrelated workspace-wide work for task-backed failures. One medium-severity finding was submitted.

Scenarios.Scenario: A task-backed subagent is cancelled, or a taskless subagent reports `completed(cancelled: true)`
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Task-backed cancellation uses the existing reconciled task snapshot; taskless runtime cancellation enters the existing quiet-period scheduler. The changed path emits `ChatTurnCancelled` before `subagent_completed`, synchronously ending the child state. Cancellation-specific checkpoint discard and contribution work are asynchronous/off the immediate completion path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Lists background tasks for authoritative task-backed cancellation state.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One effective reconciled read after throttling/supersession per terminal confirmation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Cancellation already used the same task-list reconciliation; only the emitted terminal outcome changed.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Refreshes Git state and may perform a pull-request lookup for the owning session.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One trigger per newly emitted child cancellation, with overlapping work throttled/serialized per session.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: These child cancellation cases were finalized by `subagent_completed` as success and did not run the cancellation `turnEnd` pipeline.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the immediate child completion path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of cancelled child chats in a parent session. Each child has one active terminal action because `_settleSubagentTurn` removes it before the following completion signal.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Task reconciliation remains serialized. Checkpoint discard is sequenced per parent session. Git-state refreshes caused by the generic `turnEnd` contribution are throttled/serialized per resolved session key.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Pending lifecycle outcome and completion scheduler entries are deleted by `_completeSubagentTurn`. Cancelled turn IDs remain until parent-session removal, matching the retained child-chat lifetime; no standalone unbounded resource was established. Git state is cached but refresh queries are throttled rather than eliminated.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the extra terminal action and Git refresh trigger; moderate impact because refresh throttling limits bursts.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Most overlapping cancellations are bounded by Git refresh throttling, and cancellation skips checkpoint/changeset capture, so the remaining incremental cost is smaller than the failed-task path.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate finding: this is the same generic child terminal-action fan-out root cause as the reported failed-subagent issue, with lower incremental cost and no evidence warranting a duplicate comment.

Scenarios.Scenario: A task-backed subagent becomes idle/completed successfully, or a taskless failure follows the pre-existing lifecycle event path
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Successful task snapshots still settle after the existing task-list confirmation and emit only `subagent_completed`. A taskless explicit failure still emits the same `ChatError` it emitted before this PR, now represented by the outcome union.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Reads the task list to confirm successful terminal status.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing throttled reconciliations; no new calls from the outcome representation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical task-list reads and completion scheduling.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of completed children or taskless explicit failures; no changed multiplicity was found for these cases.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Existing per-child schedulers and the shared task reconciliation throttler remain unchanged.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Schedulers, pending lifecycle entries, activity revisions, and token-usage maps are cleaned on completion as before. Warm/cold behavior is unchanged.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material for PR causality; the outcome type change is allocation-neutral at realistic scale.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance regression: successful completion behavior is unchanged, and taskless failure already used the error action path before this PR.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all three changed files and traced child failure, cancellation, and success paths through task RPC reconciliation, state routing, contributions, Git/diff/database boundaries, cleanup, coalescing, and concurrency. One medium-severity boundary-fanout regression was reported for task-backed failures entering workspace-wide turn-end processing.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
